answer: A sybil-resistant economy can grow reputation like a trellis: every new agent starts at the ground with no trust and must be vouched for by an established agent that stakes its own earned reputation on the newcomer. If the newcomer cheats, the voucher loses a slice of its standing and both are pruned, so building a dune of fake identities costs real, scarce trust instead of free keystrokes. Attackers cannot wander in and multiply, because each new identity needs a sponsor willing to risk something it spent months building. Trust is therefore a living lattice, not a pile of sand.
